threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, inspection, editing, revision-resolution and rendering engine, exposed through a native CLI, PyO3 Python bindings, wasm-bindgen Node/browser bindings, and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Documents flow from caller-owned bytes or local files through ZIP/OPC admission, XML/DOM processing, comparison/edit/layout components, then back to bytes, stdout or explicitly selected output paths. Python and WASM reuse the root engine with default features disabled, excluding its self-updater (README.md:14-18; src/lib.rs:96-165; jubarte-python/Cargo.toml:35-39; jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-32). MCP grants a persistent filesystem capability rooted at --root, defaulting to startup cwd (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381). Native rendering independently discovers host fonts and maintains a font index outside that document-root capability (src/convert/mod.rs:806-857; src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3106,3213-3227). Native self-update and maintainer release/publication are conditional privileged workflows (src/update.rs:186-257; scripts/release.sh:875-919; .github/workflows/release.yml:230-269).
assets: Confidential document text, comments, revisions, embedded media/fonts and metadata; emitted Markdown, snapshots, patches, reports, PDFs and PNGs can contain that content. MCP reads return document content; edit/render writes named artifacts (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,185-217,234-255).

Integrity of source snapshots and authorized clean/tracked output. V1 plans optionally bind source_sha256; V2 requires matching source.sha256. Native CLI rechecks named source against preparation bytes (src/edit.rs:99-106,2073-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-99; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655).

Host CPU, memory and filesystem authority exercised by parsers, image/font decoders and publication. Default admission permits 64 MiB compressed/per part, 256 MiB total inflated, 10,000 entries and depth 256; comparison permits 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB total (src/admission.rs:63-99).

MCP root document/output files; native host fonts, user font folders and font-index.tsv are separately authorized resources (src/publication.rs:146-199; src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315,2637-2652,3100-3106).

Installed native executable and package integrity. Updater currently trusts release-adjacent SHA256SUMS.txt; compiled signing keys are empty and first-signed-release is None (src/update.rs:25-48,198-210,245-257).

Distinct publication credentials: CI ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, release-job GITHUB_TOKEN, operator Cargo credentials, npm login/NPM_OTP and UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN (.github/workflows/release.yml:234-235,261-290,356-369; scripts/release.sh:374-380,919,934-956,1069).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted DOCX crosses ZIP/OPC admission: pre-index budgets, ZIP structural/canonical-name checks, encryption/compression refusal, bounded inflation and XML policy (src/admission.rs:439-569). OPC independently checks archive defects, bounded reads and case-insensitive duplicates (src/opc/archive.rs:34-51; src/opc/mod.rs:282-350,497-524). Rendering admits before normalization/layout (src/convert/mod.rs:769-798).

Raw XML parse_xdocument intentionally skips input policy; try_parse_xdocument_with_limits validates first. Callers of raw API own prior admission (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:88-135). Tag defaults are 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte names, 64 MiB values and 128 MiB tags (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-65).

Edit plans cross into mutation using schema/source checks, exact anchors and preparation gates; author labels are not authenticated identities. V1 rejects macro-bearing/signed packages and checks optional source hash; V2 rejects mismatching source hash before operation resolution (src/edit.rs:97-108,2073-2105; src/edit/v2_apply.rs:84-111).

Native CLI uses ambient operator filesystem authority. publish_paths holds parents, stages/verifies bytes and installs via overwrite rename or no-clobber hard link, atomic per file rather than per set (src/publication.rs:168-174,203-225,419-505,534-570). Python/Node ordinary CLI path writes have different controls (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-80,106-111).

MCP client arguments cross a server-granted directory capability. Startup resolves --root once; diagnostics precede capability-relative actual reads/writes. Portable relative-name checks, overwrite opt-in and output-symlink refusal apply (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-273,431-463). All connected stdio clients receive registered tools; annotations are hints rather than per-user authorization (mcp_server.py:54-55,126-159,258-277, relative to jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines).

Native Markdown image loading separately grants --resource-path, otherwise Markdown parent or '.'. Percent decoding precedes scheme/containment checks and capability reads; operator chooses trusted root (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2877,2936-2943). Python/Node reject resource_path; byte conversion defaults to no image callback (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:1057-1064; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:724-727; src/markdown/mod.rs:159-198,226).

Native font discovery reads system/Word, macOS Office CloudFonts/<family>, and configured/per-user fonts. Cloud family must be a single normal component. Index-named files are read after length/mtime checks; ambient cache persistence is independent of MCP root (src/convert/mod.rs:806-857; src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2258-2315,2637-2652,2855-2862,3154-3188,3213-3227).
Maintainer debug intentionally uses open_archive_unchecked after budget preflight, reports defects and continues, unlike ordinary refusal paths (src/debug.rs:206-222; src/opc/archive.rs:15-19).

Native updater downloads fixed repository/platform release assets, checks adjacent checksum and extracted regular-file type, and requires terminal confirmation or --yes; --check does not install. Empty signing keys disable required signatures (src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,198-257,299-320).

Tag CI separates read-only build from contents:write release. Signing-step secret is decoded below RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and cleaned on exit. Separate GitHub token publishes dist/*; operator script independently publishes Cargo, npm engine/CLI and PyPI (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,54-55,230-290,303-321,356-369; scripts/release.sh:875-919,934-956,1039-1069).

Contributor pull_request jobs check out contributor code onto self-hosted runners also selected by main pushes; their local action configures a private mbx cache endpoint and documents persistent checkout/store use (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-16,34-48,72-99; .github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-12,20-38). External approval and runner isolation controls remain unknown.

Legacy DOC crosses OLE/FIB/piece decoding then field-block processing before Markdown/DOCX generation; physical chain bounds do not establish logical story or field-work limits (src/legacy_doc.rs:180-215,1090-1225,1596-1619). Embedded WMF crosses binary record decoding to owned text and raster output; MAX_SIDE bounds only pixels (src/convert/metafile.rs:25-31,477-489,603-620,692-700).

CLI/library callers already control invocation and explicitly supplied paths under their OS account; escalation requires authority beyond these grants (src/publication.rs:203-225; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2866). A separate local principal may control entries in a shared output/plan directory.

Release/registry/signing compromise is separate authority; checksum-only updates do not authenticate against a compiled key, but document control does not imply release control (src/update.rs:44-48,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80).

Public-service/tenant effects require deployment separation not established by inspected source; no public HTTP service was established (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381; SECURITY.md:84-85).

MCP says tools only touch files under root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:7-9,67-68), but render calls native installed-font discovery and index persistence outside that root (same file:234-236; src/convert/mod.rs:857; src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3106,3183-3188,3213-3227). It is not inside fonts nor necessarily MCP root; temporary sibling is font-index.tsv.<PID>.tmp (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3106,3213-3227).

Fixed repository is jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines, current control TLS/checksum/regular-file check/confirmation. SELF_UPDATE says GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN lift rate limits (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24), but updater never opts into environment-token loading (src/update.rs:198-211). Architecture reviewer inspected locked self_update 1.3.1 default auth_token=None/auth_token_from_env=false and token copying; supporting cached dependency src/backends/common.rs:1027-1053,1077-1085 and src/macros.rs:580; repository Cargo.lock:2552-2553. Documentation/availability discrepancy, not evidence of leakage.

Frontend common flags do not establish identical filesystem controls: Python/Node ordinary output uses host path APIs and rejects unsupported capabilities; WASM has no native OutputRoot module/dependency, Node filesystem belongs to JS host (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-133,1048-1073; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:6-14,76-80,106-111,724-740; Cargo.toml:173-177; src/lib.rs:160-165).

CI signing receives only ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY in the signing shell/zipsign process, stores decoded keys under RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN, validates 64-byte keys, cleans on exit and signs dist/jubarte-*.tar.gz/zip; verification uses committed keys when present. Operator Cargo publication uses Cargo-owned credentials/CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN and confirmation/release gates; npm engine jubarte-wasm and CLI jubarte-redlines publish independently under npm login and optional NPM_OTP; PyPI uses UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN and validated complete CI wheels/sdist, with explicit --no-wait for local partial fallback (scripts/release.sh:363-380,875-959,1039-1069). Secret scopes and actual provider accounts are external.
Release script selects an external application checkout via JUBARTE_APP_DIR or jubarte-app; its implementation is outside scope and uninspected (scripts/release.sh:382-387).

findings.title: DOCX and HTML table spans cause unbounded renderer expansion
findings.summary: A small DOCX can set w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter to an enormous positive integer. Rendering expands the table column vector to the attacker-provided occupancy without a semantic column budget, causing excessive allocation or a process-terminating allocation failure. ZIP size and XML nesting admission do not bound these numeric values. Internal HTML altChunk colspan values independently expand into one generated w:gridCol per requested column before the generated XML is parsed, bypassing the original package's byte budgets.

severity.rationale: An attacker who can supply a document to a rendering caller can reliably request allocations disproportionate to input size and terminate or exhaust that process. No authentication bypass, code execution, remote service deployment or host-wide outage is established.
severity.changeConditions: Process memory/CPU limits and per-request process isolation confine impact; a shared long-lived renderer increases availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source traces the unbounded usize from XML through RawCell.colspan and occupancy into vec!/resize after admission. No runtime reproduction was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded table span from document XML
codeEvidence.explanation: The return type is usize; positive values have no upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: Row grid skip uses the same unchecked span
codeEvidence.explanation: Both gridBefore and gridAfter become RawCell.colspan at line 14379 and reach the same occupancy allocator.

codeEvidence.label: Occupancy directly sizes column storage
codeEvidence.explanation: A single span of 1,000,000,000 requests at least four billion bytes of f32 columns before later per-column allocations.

codeEvidence.label: Public rendering uses admission before table construction
codeEvidence.explanation: Ordinary valid small table XML is reachable through public PDF/PNG/render-report APIs; archive/XML admission does not cap table column values.

codeEvidence.label: HTML spans generate proportional XML without a budget
codeEvidence.explanation: The maximum row span sum drives generated XML size. The HTML parser accepts positive usize colspan without a maximum at lines 562-566; expansion is called after original package admission at convert/mod.rs:789-798.

rootCause.summary: The renderer treats document-controlled span counts as allocation sizes without a maximum semantic table width or checked aggregate occupancy. The HTML table importer likewise accepts unbounded colspan and materializes a grid proportional to it before DOM parsing.

findings.remediation: Introduce a configurable maximum table-column/occupancy budget, validate gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter before constructing cells, use checked_add for aggregate spans, and reject excessive values with a typed conversion error before allocating. Apply the same budget to all table sources. Enforce the same maximum during HTML altChunk parsing and checked row-span accumulation, and cap generated XML/output before materialization.

counterEvidence: Package admission runs first and rejects malformed/over-budget ZIP/XML; a tiny valid numeric span is within those checks.
SECURITY.md recommends process memory/CPU limits; these constrain blast radius but do not prevent request-triggered renderer termination.
limitations: No application execution, exploit input creation, or runtime memory measurement.
Actual shared-service deployment and isolation are unknown.
validation.summary: Parent verified the positive usize parser, row skip sibling, RawCell propagation, occupancy allocator and public with_layout entry path. Admission limits are byte/entry/depth/attribute budgets (src/admission.rs:42-99), not table-column bounds. Parent also verified altchunk::expand -> html_to_wml -> end_table, its positive usize colspan parser and unbounded gridCol generation. Both paths require the same semantic table-column budget; original package admission precedes HTML expansion.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> with_layout admission/normalization -> DOM body table -> table_block -> cell_span or row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> cols vec!/resize. Alternate path: internal altChunk relationship -> package HTML bytes -> html_to_wml colspan -> end_table gridCol loop -> generated XML -> DOM/layout.

impact.rationale: Loss of availability of the rendering process.

likelihood.rationale: A small document carries a representable large positive span; no unusual configuration is needed.

reachability.summary: Public docx_to_pdf/docx_to_png/render/docx_render_report render caller-supplied DOCX bytes; the table is constructed before PDF/PNG output limits.
reachability.attacker: A document author able to get a caller to render their DOCX.
reachability.outcome: Memory exhaustion or renderer process termination.
preconditions: Victim renders attacker-controlled DOCX content.

attackPath.summary: Untrusted document author crosses the document-to-renderer resource boundary through semantic table counts.

remediationTests: Test boundary and over-limit gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter via public rendering APIs; assert bounded refusal without allocating attacker-sized storage.
Test combined row spans and arithmetic overflow; preserve ordinary merged-cell rendering.

Rendering expands the table column vector to the attacker-provided occupancy without a semantic column budget, causing excessive allocation or a process-terminating allocation failure. ZIP size and XML nesting admission do not bound these numeric values. Internal HTML altChunk colspan values independently expand into one generated w:gridCol per requested column before the generated XML is parsed, bypassing the original package's byte budgets.

severity.rationale: An attacker who can supply a document to a rendering caller can reliably request allocations disproportionate to input size and terminate or exhaust that process. No authentication bypass, code execution, remote service deployment or host-wide outage is established.
severity.changeConditions: Process memory/CPU limits and per-request process isolation confine impact; a shared long-lived renderer increases availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source traces the unbounded usize from XML through RawCell.colspan and occupancy into vec!/resize after admission. No runtime reproduction was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded table span from document XML
codeEvidence.explanation: The return type is usize; positive values have no upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: Row grid skip uses the same unchecked span
codeEvidence.explanation: Both gridBefore and gridAfter become RawCell.colspan at line 14379 and reach the same occupancy allocator.

codeEvidence.label: Occupancy directly sizes column storage
codeEvidence.explanation: A single span of 1,000,000,000 requests at least four billion bytes of f32 columns before later per-column allocations.

codeEvidence.label: Public rendering uses admission before table construction
codeEvidence.explanation: Ordinary valid small table XML is reachable through public PDF/PNG/render-report APIs; archive/XML admission does not cap table column values.

codeEvidence.label: HTML spans generate proportional XML without a budget
codeEvidence.explanation: The maximum row span sum drives generated XML size. The HTML parser accepts positive usize colspan without a maximum at lines 562-566; expansion is called after original package admission at convert/mod.rs:789-798.

rootCause.summary: The renderer treats document-controlled span counts as allocation sizes without a maximum semantic table width or checked aggregate occupancy. The HTML table importer likewise accepts unbounded colspan and materializes a grid proportional to it before DOM parsing.

previousFindings.remediation: Introduce a configurable maximum table-column/occupancy budget, validate gridSpan/gridBefore/gridAfter before constructing cells, use checked_add for aggregate spans, and reject excessive values with a typed conversion error before allocating. Apply the same budget to all table sources. Enforce the same maximum during HTML altChunk parsing and checked row-span accumulation, and cap generated XML/output before materialization.

counterEvidence: Package admission runs first and rejects malformed/over-budget ZIP/XML; a tiny valid numeric span is within those checks.
SECURITY.md recommends process memory/CPU limits; these constrain blast radius but do not prevent request-triggered renderer termination.
limitations: No application execution, exploit input creation, or runtime memory measurement.
Actual shared-service deployment and isolation are unknown.
validation.summary: Parent verified the positive usize parser, row skip sibling, RawCell propagation, occupancy allocator and public with_layout entry path. Parent also verified altchunk::expand -> html_to_wml -> end_table, its positive usize colspan parser and unbounded gridCol generation. Both paths require the same semantic table-column budget; original package admission precedes HTML expansion.

likelihood.rationale: A small document carries a representable large positive span; no unusual configuration is needed.

findings.title: Predictable plan and font-cache staging paths follow local symlinks
findings.summary: The Python and npm CLIs record edit plans through .<plan-name>.<pid>.partial using ordinary truncating writes. A different local user able to create entries in the plan directory can preplant that name as a symlink to another file writable by the victim; the write truncates and replaces the referent's contents before the rename. The native CLI uses exclusive private staging and does not share this failure. The native font-index writer has the same mechanism when a trusted operator configures its cache parent as a directory writable by another principal (JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX or shared user-font location). Its default per-user cache does not establish that prerequisite.

severity.rationale: This is a conditional local integrity issue requiring a shared attacker-writable plan directory and prediction or observation of the CLI PID. It can overwrite unrelated files with the validated JSON plan using victim privileges; remote reachability and code execution are not established.
severity.changeConditions: Private plan directories remove the attacker prerequisite; use by a more privileged victim in a shared writable directory increases impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source shows predictable PID names and symlink-following truncating Path.write_bytes/fs.writeFileSync calls. No runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.code:
target = Path(os.path.realpath(plan))
        partial = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.{os.getpid()}.partial")
        try:
            partial.write_bytes(recorded["json"].encode("utf-8"))
            os.replace(partial, target)
codeEvidence.explanation: Realpath resolves the plan, not its newly derived partial sibling. write_bytes opens and truncates an existing symlink referent.

codeEvidence.label: Font index uses a predictable truncating temporary write
codeEvidence.explanation: A preplanted temporary-path symlink redirects fs::write before the rename. This requires a cache parent writable by a distinct attacker; default private per-user cache is counterevidence.

rootCause.summary: Two host CLI writers construct predictable temporary filenames and open them with truncation instead of exclusively creating private staging files. The same predictable, nonexclusive pattern occurs in the native persistent font index.

findings.remediation: Route Python recording through the existing native exclusive publication function. For npm, exclusively create a randomly named private staging directory/file in the plan parent, write and verify through a held descriptor, then atomically rename. Refuse existing staging names and avoid following links. Apply exclusive private staging to FontIndex::save as well, and keep shared cache storage segregated by OS principal.

counterEvidence: Victim chooses the plan path and no remote service is established.
Private per-user directories prevent another principal from planting the partial name.
Plan generation and preview validate document operations, but neither checks the staging inode.
Default font-cache parent is per-user; a shared configured parent is an explicit extra prerequisite, and same-user self-only control is not an escalation.
limitations: Requires shared writable directory and a different principal who can precreate the predictable name.
The overwritten data is valid plan JSON, not arbitrary binary payload; no execution outcome established.
validation.summary: Parent verified both record entrypaths, preview/dry-run gates, realpath handling, default file-write semantics, and native sibling counterevidence. A pre-existing partial symlink is not checked or opened exclusively. Parent verified installed_family_faces/cjk_family_faces -> indexed_faces -> record -> save; index path is configuration/per-user derived. Font cache is conditionally affected only if a different principal can create its temporary sibling.

findings.title: Unbounded numbering levels exhaust renderer CPU and memory
findings.summary: A DOCX paragraph may specify any u32 numbering level. Resolving an undefined large level searches every lower integer; defining that large level instead initializes a counter for every lower level and later scans each placeholder level. A tiny document can therefore trigger billions of iterations or counter entries after normal package admission.

severity.rationale: A document author can cause severe per-process availability loss through ordinary rendering. A shared remotely reachable service is not assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Per-request CPU/memory limits and process isolation bound the outage; shared rendering hosts increase availability impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct static source shows uncapped u32 input driving integer ranges and map allocation. The caller chain is list_marker -> next_revised -> next_marker/resolve_ilvl. Runtime reproduction was not performed.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded document level
codeEvidence.explanation: No semantic maximum is enforced before callers resolve or iterate over the level.

codeEvidence.label: Integer-range fallback search
codeEvidence.code:
(0..ilvl)
            .rev()
            .find(|i| lvls.contains_key(i))
            .unwrap_or(ilvl)
codeEvidence.explanation: With only level zero defined and ilvl 4294967295, this attempts roughly 4.3 billion lookups.

codeEvidence.label: Counters materialized for every lower integer
codeEvidence.explanation: Defining the attacker-selected large level avoids fallback but reaches this proportional map expansion.

rootCause.summary: Numbering metadata is accepted as arbitrary u32 and used as the extent of dense scans and counter materialization, without validating the supported level range.

findings.remediation: Validate numbering levels at every paragraph/style/abstract/override parse against the supported bounded range. Select existing lower levels by bounded/sparse map lookup rather than walking arbitrary integer ranges, and materialize only necessary bounded counters; return a typed error for unsupported metadata.

counterEvidence: Admission bounds compressed/inflated bytes and XML shape but not ilvl values.
An undefined list instance returns early; the attacker can include a normal matching num/abstractNum relationship.
Process isolation recommended in SECURITY.md can bound impact.
limitations: No runtime timing or allocation measurement; actual hosting deployment unknown.
validation.summary: Parent verified paragraph parsing, explicitly defined level parsing at 6618-6644, list_marker/next_revised/next_marker calls, fallback search, dense counter initialization and render placeholder scan. A tiny ordinary package passes byte/depth limits while carrying the oversized integer.

findings.title: ZIP entry-count admission can inspect a different EOCD record than the ZIP reader
findings.summary: The pre-index entry budget reads the last raw EOCD signature and trusts its count without validating that record. The pinned ZIP reader searches candidate end records and falls back when decoding a candidate fails. A misleading later EOCD can therefore pass the precheck with a low count while the reader indexes an earlier valid archive with more entries. Admission checks only for fewer indexed entries than declared, leaving the configured maximum unenforced against the actual index.

severity.rationale: An untrusted package can bypass the caller's entry-count resource boundary and force indexing/processing beyond its configured maximum. Compressed-byte and inflated-byte budgets still apply, so unlimited input or arbitrary execution is not claimed.
severity.changeConditions: Use a single validated EOCD interpretation for budget and reader, bound index construction, and verify actual archive length against max_entries before further work. Process resource isolation limits impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source establishes the raw-signature precheck, dependency fallback loop and missing actual upper-bound check. No crafted archive was created or executed, so exact fallback behavior for a concrete file remains unmeasured.

codeEvidence.label: Post-open validation has no actual-count upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: The reader's final archive count is checked only for being smaller than declared; larger actual counts are not compared to max_entries.

rootCause.summary: Resource admission and ZIP parsing do not share a validated end-record decision; a one-sided post-open comparison cannot enforce the upper bound against the reader's actual entry index.

findings.remediation: Resolve end records once with validation matching the ZIP reader and enforce the selected entry count before index allocation. Also compare archive.len() with max_entries after opening as defense in depth. Refuse ambiguous mismatches instead of trusting a raw signature hit.

counterEvidence: Compressed size and inflated bytes remain bounded; this bypass specifically concerns entry-count/indexing work.
Malformed metadata may be refused by the reader; the differential needs a later rejected candidate plus an earlier valid archive.
The structural pass checks actual local/central records, overlaps and special types, but does not restore the pre-index count budget.
limitations: No concrete archive/runtime validation was performed; exploit reliability is medium confidence.
An actual upper-bound check after opening would stop later processing but cannot by itself prevent over-budget index allocation.
